source_text: Multa sine voluntate Dei geruntur, nihil sine providentia. Indicat Deus quae velit affectu hominibus noto — ideo locutus dicitur. Non os corporeum, sed voluntas menti illuminatae formata in verba.
pass_a_gloss: Many-things without will of-God are-done, nothing without providence. Indicates God what he-wills by-affect to-humans known — therefore spoken he-is-said. Not mouth bodily, but will to-mind illuminated formed into words.
pass_b_english: Many things happen without God’s will; nothing without his providence. God shows what he wills by an affect humans know — so he is said to have spoken. Not a bodily mouth, but a will shaped into words in an illuminated mind.
